stemMd: According to the passage, why do lichens readily absorb pollutants?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They have no roots or waxy skin, so they take in water and dissolved substances over their whole surface.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Their algal partner needs sulphur dioxide in order to photosynthesise.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Their fungal partner stores gases in its structure.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They depend on nitrogen for their food supply.

options.label: E
options.textMd: They grow mainly on tree trunks close to busy roads.

explanationMd:
Go to the first paragraph and read the sentence that gives the reason: "Because a lichen has no roots and no waxy skin, it takes in water and dissolved substances over its whole surface, straight from rain and air." That is the mechanism, and it is why the passage calls the lichen "an excellent sponge for nutrients and ... for pollutants".

The other choices borrow words from the passage (fungus, alga, sulphur dioxide, tree trunks, nitrogen) and attach them to claims the passage does not make. When a choice sounds scientific but you cannot find it in the text, it does not count.

distractorRationale.c: The fungus is said to give the lichen its structure. Nothing is said about storing gases.
distractorRationale.b: The alga is said to supply food. The passage never says it needs sulphur dioxide; on the contrary, the gas makes sensitive species disappear.
distractorRationale.e: The passage says lichens were recorded on tree trunks at a series of sites, not that they grow mainly near busy roads; vehicle exhausts come up only as a source of nitrogen that favours some species.
distractorRationale.d: Only some species are described as thriving on nitrogen, and food comes from the algal partner. Neither explains why lichens absorb pollutants.

accessibilityText: A stated-information question about the lichen passage. It asks why lichens readily absorb pollutants. The five choices: they have no roots or waxy skin, so they take in water and dissolved substances over their whole surface; their algal partner needs sulphur dioxide to photosynthesise; their fungal partner stores gases in its structure; they depend on nitrogen for their food supply; they grow mainly on tree trunks close to busy roads.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Paragraph 1 says it directly: with no roots and no waxy skin, a lichen takes in water and dissolved substances over its whole surface. B, C and D invent mechanisms, and D confuses the nitrogen-loving species with the general cause. E is not stated as the reason. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: This is a direct restatement of paragraph 1: no roots and no waxy skin, so the lichen absorbs over its whole surface. The passage never says the algal partner needs SO2 (B) or that the fungus stores gases (C). D wrongly generalises from the nitrogen-loving species to all lichens. E is not the stated cause.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: the first paragraph gives the reason in one sentence; each other choice attaches passage vocabulary to a claim the text does not make. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
